title: Waffle
description: Light and crisp homemade waffles with a fluffy interior, perfect for breakfast or dessert. Serve warm with your favorite toppings for a classic Continental treat.

ingredients.title: For the Waffle Batter
items: Unsalted butter – ½ cup (115 g), melted
Optional: Cinnamon – ¼ tsp for subtle warmth

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Dry Ingredients
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon (if using).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prepare the Wet Ingredients
steps: In another bowl, whisk together egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract until smooth.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Whip the Egg Whites
steps: In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form. This gives the waffle extra lightness.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Combine Batter
steps: Slowly fold the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Gently fold in the whipped egg whites, keeping as much air as possible.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Cook the Waffles
steps: Preheat your waffle iron and lightly grease with butter or oil.
Pour batter into the iron (usually about ¾ cup per waffle, depending on size).
Cook for 4–6 minutes, until golden brown and crisp.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Serve
steps: Serve immediately for the best texture.
Optional toppings: fresh berries, whipped cream, maple syrup, chocolate sauce, or a dusting of powdered sugar.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with fresh berries and whipped cream.
Drizzle with maple syrup or chocolate sauce.
Finish with a dusting of powdered sugar.

chefTips: For crispier waffles, use a bit more melted butter or a touch of cornstarch in the flour.
Folding in the whipped egg whites at the end makes a noticeably fluffier interior.
Keep cooked waffles warm in a 90°C (200°F) oven on a rack to keep them crisp without steaming.
Serve with a small quenelle of butter or a drizzle of sauce for restaurant-quality plating.
